_doc: Single source of truth for the Physically Anchored Adaptive PUEA experiments. Every experimental constant lives here; Python modules only read it. Units: positions in metres inside an area_size x area_size square, powers in dBm, gains/offsets in dB. See docs/adaptive_puea.md for the meaning of each block.

regimes._doc: Each regime re-runs every scenario with the listed overrides deep-merged into this config. 'default' is the easy case for the physical anchor (40 SUs, 4 dB shadowing); 'weak_anchor' is a regime where the anchor's spatial resolution is poor (see resolution_sweep), so the other components must carry more of the work.

geometry._doc: SUs are placed uniformly at random (per seed). Distances are clipped at min_su_distance to keep the path-loss model finite.

channel._doc: Pr = Pt * r^(-alpha) * exp(a*beta), a = ln(10)/10, beta ~ N(0, shadow_sigma_db^2) (Chhetry & Marchang, 2021). Measured energy = Pr + noise. shadow_time_correlation is the AR(1) coefficient of each link's shadowing across slots (0 = i.i.d. as in the baseline paper). shadow_decorrelation_distance (m): the attacker's per-link shadowing is correlated with the PU's by c = exp(-|x_att - x_PU| / d) (Gudmundson-type exponential model, d of the order of 10-50 m in the measurement literature); without it a co-located attacker would see shadowing independent of the PU's, which is physically wrong and lets a sequential test exploit PU/attacker switching when shadowing is correlated in time.

attacker._doc: Default attacker operating point. basic_power_dbm is deliberately NOT power-matched; power-matched variants compute their power from the geometry (see simulation/scenarios.py::matched_power_dbm).

streams._doc: Calibration = PU-only stable stream (thresholds, alpha/sigma estimates, initial profile). XGBoost training = stable PU slots + generic attackers at uniformly random positions (>= min distance from PU) with power = matched power + U(offset range). Test streams use independent random streams.

power_drift.description: PU transmit power ramps +6 dB (x4) between slots 400 and 1400.

shadowing_drift.description: Shadowing std ramps 4.0 -> 5.5 dB between slots 400 and 1400.

noise_drift.description: Noise floor rises +4 dB between slots 400 and 1400.

combined_drift.description: Power +4 dB, shadowing +1 dB, noise +3 dB, all ramped between slots 400 and 1400.

basic_puea.description: Attacker at basic_xy with basic_power_dbm transmits in 30% of slots after slot 500.

power_matching_puea.description: Attacker at basic_xy chooses its power so its mean RSS over the SUs equals the PU's (assumes it knows SU positions and alpha).

gradual_puea.description: Open-loop evasion: PU-likeness q steps through the stages; q moves the attacker from basic_xy toward a point min_distance_to_pu from the PU and moves its power from basic_power_dbm to the matched power.

stealthy_puea.description: Adaptive attacker placed distance_from_pu from the PU that tracks the PU's (drifting) power every slot and transmits rarely. PU has a +6 dB power drift.

poisoning.description: Closed-loop boiling-frog poisoning. Phase 1 (slots < poison_start): PU only. Phase 2: attacker injects poison in poison_rate of slots with progress p in [0,1] interpolating from a PU-mimic (start_distance_from_pu from the PU, power-matched) to the target (basic_xy, basic_power_dbm); p increases by step_up when the slot was NOT flagged (SUs vacated) and decreases by step_down when flagged. Phase 3 (slots >= attack_start): attacker transmits at the target in attack_rate of slots.

near_pu_poisoning.description: Closed-loop poisoning inside the anchor's resolution limit: poison starts 3 m from the PU and the target is 8 m from the PU (toward basic_xy) at matched power + 8 dB.

slow_near_pu_poisoning.description: Low-duty-cycle version of near_pu_poisoning: poison injected in only 5% of slots (minimises the sequential test's evidence per slot), same start/target points and attack phase.

resolution_sweep._doc: Anchor-resolution experiment: a power-matched attacker at distance d from the PU (random directions inside the area) transmits every slot of a short stream; we record the fraction of its slots rejected by the physical check (calibrated on PU-only data for the same geometry and channel). Answers: how close must an attacker be to defeat the anchor, and how does that depend on shadowing and the number of SUs?

features._doc: Fusion-center-observable features per slot (see src/fc_features.py): the 5 statistics of Chhetry & Marchang computed over the SU RSS vector in dBm, plus mean SNR.

xgboost._doc: Hyperparameters copied verbatim from src/train_ensemble.py::train_xgboost so the simulated baseline is the same learner as the repository baseline.

physical_consistency._statistic_doc: 'glrt': Lambda = n*ln(SSR_pu / SSR_min) comparing a fit at the known PU location against the best grid location (sigma-free). 'chi2': SSR_pu / sigma_hat^2 / (n-1) (requires sigma, sensitive to shadowing drift).
physical_consistency._threshold_doc: Threshold = empirical (1 - calibration_false_alarm) quantile of the statistic on the held-out half of the PU-only calibration stream. Never uses test data.

adaptive_profile._doc: Initial mean/covariance from MinCovDet on the first half of the calibration stream; the Mahalanobis threshold is the empirical (1 - calibration_false_alarm) quantile of d^2 on the second half. Updates are EWMA with ewma_lambda.

sequential._doc: Sequential drift-invariant location test (src/sequential_spatial.py). window: GLR-CUSUM window in verifiable slots. pfa_per_slot: probability under H0 that the statistic exceeds the threshold in a given slot (threshold by Monte Carlo on N(0, I_2), mc_seed fixed). sigma_lambda: EWMA rate of the shadowing-variance tracker, set equal to adaptive_profile.ewma_lambda so both adaptive components forget at the same rate. Attribution: mixture fit over a coarse grid (coarse_step, the physical-check grid step) plus a fine grid within local_radius of the PU; refitted every refit_every slots while the alarm is on, once at least min_slots_for_fit slots have accumulated since the change point. snapshot_every: profile checkpoint spacing for rollback. An alarm episode opens when the statistic exceeds the threshold and closes after `window` consecutive slots below it (hysteresis added after the first evaluation; see docs/adaptive_puea.md section 11).

evaluation._doc: rolling_window: window for rolling FPR/recall curves and adaptation recovery. oracle_window: trailing window over the evaluation-only oracle PU features used as the true legitimate profile mean. Recovery (settling time) = slots from drift onset to the LAST slot at which the rolling FPR exceeds recovery_fpr_tolerance (0 if never exceeded; not recovered if still above at the end of the stream). The tolerance is set well above the ~1-2% calibrated FPR so chance excursions of a 100-slot window rarely trigger it.
